name: רֵכָב
summary: Best known as the father of Jehonadab (Jonadab) son of Rechab, whom Jehu met on the road, took up into his chariot (הַמֶּרְכָּבָה) and had ride with him to see his zeal for Yahweh (2Ki 10:15–16, 23); Jonadab commanded his sons to drink no wine, build no house, sow no seed and plant no vineyard but live in tents, and Jeremiah set the obedience of the house of the Rechabites (הָרֵכָבִים) against Judah's disobedience, with Yahweh's promise that Jonadab son of Rechab would not lack a man to stand before him for ever (Jer 35:2–19). The house of Rechab is traced to Hammath of the Kenites (1Ch 2:55). The name is also borne by Rechab son of Rimmon the Beerothite, a captain of Ish-bosheth's raiding bands who with his brother Baanah murdered him and was put to death by David (2Sa 4:2–12), and by the father of Malchijah, ruler of the district of Beth-haccerem, who repaired the Dung Gate (Neh 3:14). The name has the consonants of the verb רָכַב “ride” and reads as “rider”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Jehonadab son of רֵכָב … and he took him up to him into the chariot.”
“Come with me and see my zeal for Yahweh; and they made him ride (וַיַּרְכִּבוּ) in his chariot.”
“Go to the house of the Rechabites (הָרֵכָבִים) and speak to them.”
“Jonadab son of Rechab our father commanded us, You shall drink no wine … and you shall build no house … but dwell in tents all your days.”
“Jonadab son of Rechab shall not lack a man to stand before me for ever.”
“The Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.”
“The name of the one was Baanah and the name of the second רֵכָב, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite.”
“Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccerem, repaired the Dung Gate.”
רָכַב “ride”, the verb the name's consonants spell: “he rode on it.”

note: Takes t.cq.af (the name, 13 tokens) and t.cq.ag (the gentilic הָרֵכָבִים, Jer 35:2, 3, 5, 18; TIPNR files it under Rechab@2Ki.10.15 as “Group”). The brief's 1Ch 4:12 token under t.cq.ag is רֵכָה, the place Recah, left unassigned in rakav. TIPNR tags 1Ch 2:55's “house of Rechab” under the same Rechab as Jonadab's father; whether Malchijah son of Rechab (Neh 3:14) is of the Rechabite house is not said. The reading “rider” takes רֵכָב as a noun of the root; the pointing differs from רַכָּב “charioteer” and no verse gives the meaning.
